blocks.orig: It can be interesting to see where young wildebeest calves are born and see the long journey the wildebeest have to travel. These are some rare sights you can find during the Great Wildebeest Migration in Tanzania and into Kenya.
blocks.html: Seeing where young wildebeest calves come into the world, and following the long journey the wildebeest must make, can be fascinating. These are rare sights you can witness during the Great Wildebeest Migration through Tanzania and on into Kenya.

blocks.orig: So, where do the 1.5 million wildebeest come from, and how many calves are born there? Read on to find out more about this magnificent event called the wildebeest calving season and what other animals are involved during this period.
blocks.html: So where do the 1.5 million wildebeest come from, and how many calves are born along the way? Keep reading to learn more about this remarkable event, known as the wildebeest calving season, and about the other animals that take part in it.

blocks.orig: We start at the southern plains of the Serengeti, where the plentiful red oat and water grass grow after the short November rain season, and we now have a full plain.
blocks.html: Our starting point is the southern plains of the Serengeti, where red oat and water grass grow in abundance after the short rains of November, and the plain is now full.

blocks.orig: From here, we can expect great waves of wildebeest to pass over the east side of the Serengeti.
blocks.html: From this point, huge waves of wildebeest can be expected to move across the eastern side of the Serengeti.

blocks.orig: The herd then goes clockwise and into nearby areas such as lake Masek and the Ngorongoro conservation area, and once the calves are born, the herd move north into Kenya’s Masai Mara.
blocks.html: Moving clockwise, the herd heads into neighbouring areas such as lake Masek and the Ngorongoro conservation area, and after the calves are born it travels north into Kenya’s Masai Mara.

blocks.orig: The area is crowded during this season because the calves can consume the richest milk, as the soil and grass are high in potassium, calcium, and phosphorus, and the short grass means predators can’t hide and attack unannounced.
blocks.html: In this season the area is packed, because the soil and grass are rich in calcium, phosphorus and potassium, which gives the calves the richest milk, and because the short grass leaves predators nowhere to hide for a surprise attack.

blocks.orig: When going north, they pass west to the Grumeti river, as it’s low, and adult wildebeests consume 3 gallons (ca. 14 litres) of water daily.
blocks.html: On their way north they head west to the Grumeti river, since it is low, and an adult wildebeest drinks 3 gallons (ca. 14 litres) of water every day.

blocks.orig: A big risk here is the crocodile-infested pools that are required to pass before they have to cross the Mara river in Kenya.
blocks.html: One major danger at this stage is the pools full of crocodiles that they must get past before crossing the Mara river in Kenya.

blocks.orig: This is a risk that comes with grazing on abundant land. During this time, they are seen continuously grazing on stocky and long grass as they need to maintain their weight for this demanding season.
blocks.html: That danger is the price of grazing on plentiful land. In this period you’ll see them grazing non-stop on long, stocky grass, because they need to keep their weight up for such a demanding season.

blocks.orig: Now we have our wildebeest herds occupying the same area in January, the pregnant wildebeest give birth, and this continues into March when as many as 8,000 calves are being born each day.
blocks.html: With the wildebeest herds sharing the same area in January, the pregnant females give birth, and this goes on into March, when up to 8,000 calves are born every day.

blocks.orig: These calves are usually born in the middle of their herds to protect the females and calves from attacks by predators, most commonly lions, cheetahs, or hyenas.
blocks.html: The calves are generally born in the centre of the herd, which protects the mothers and their young from predators, usually hyenas, cheetahs or lions.

blocks.orig: There are as many as 500,000 calves born during these months, so the herd is about to get much larger.
blocks.html: Up to 500,000 calves are born over these months, so the herd is about to grow a great deal.

blocks.orig: This culminates in over a million wildebeest, which is said to be one of the seven wonders of the natural world.
blocks.html: The result is more than a million wildebeest, a sight described as one of the seven wonders of the natural world.

blocks.orig: Amazingly, these calves learn to walk within minutes and run at full speed within an hour of being born, which makes their migration possible.
blocks.html: Remarkably, the calves can walk within minutes of birth and run at full speed within an hour, and this is what makes their migration possible.

blocks.orig: Are There Any Risks In This Calving Season?
blocks.html: Does the calving season carry any risks?

blocks.orig: Unfortunately, during the migration, the young calves can find it challenging to keep up with the older members of their group and get left behind, which is an opportunity for predators to attack.
blocks.html: Sadly, the young calves can struggle to keep pace with the older animals during the migration and fall behind, giving predators a chance to strike.

blocks.orig: In many cases, nearly 250,000 wildebeests die during this migration, and this can be due to things such as starvation, thirst, weaknesses, and climate change which can pose a threat to their survival during this season.
blocks.html: Often close to 250,000 wildebeests die during the migration, from causes such as thirst, starvation and weakness, while climate change can also threaten their survival in this season.

blocks.orig: This can involve more intense rainfall and droughts which can affect the rivers and the amount of grass there is to graze for, as wildebeests play a vital role in the sustainable renewal of the ecosystem.
blocks.html: This may mean heavier rainfall and droughts, which affect the rivers and how much grass is available for grazing, and that matters because wildebeests are vital to the sustainable renewal of the ecosystem.

blocks.orig: Tens of thousands of zebras and gazelles have already accompanied the wildebeests throughout the year.
blocks.html: All year long, the wildebeests have been joined by tens of thousands of gazelles and zebras.

blocks.orig: Here it is no exception, as they use this opportunity to birth young themselves, as the cover of many wildebeests offers great protection.
blocks.html: This stage is no different: they take the chance to give birth to their own young, since being surrounded by so many wildebeests gives them good protection.

blocks.orig: During the migration back to the northern Serengeti area and the river crossings, there can be as many as 200,000 zebras and 500,000 gazelles.
blocks.html: On the return migration to the northern Serengeti and during the river crossings, there can be up to 200,000 zebras and 500,000 gazelles.

blocks.orig: You can have over 2 million animals in this concentration, and it is even more, with 7,500 hyenas, 4,000 lions, and up to 600 cheetahs.
blocks.html: That adds up to more than 2 million animals in one concentration, and there are even more once you count the 7,500 hyenas, 4,000 lions and as many as 600 cheetahs.

blocks.orig: What’s The Best Time To See The Wildebeest Calving Season?
blocks.html: When is the best time to see the wildebeest calving season?

blocks.orig: Ideally, to observe the calving season, you want to arrange a safari somewhere between the end of December and March, as February is when the season is at its best, as there are many tented camps set up in the path of the migration.
blocks.html: To see the calving season, it is best to plan a safari for some time between late December and March; February is the peak of the season, and many tented camps are set up along the migration route.

blocks.orig: As you probably know, the great wildebeest migration happens all year round, so you can also see this amazing spectacle in central and northern Serengeti at other times of the year.
blocks.html: As you may already know, the great wildebeest migration continues all year, so you can also watch this amazing spectacle in the central and northern Serengeti at other times.

blocks.orig: If you want to see the well-known river crossing, you can visit in July and August. Our advice: a hot air balloon safari is one of the best ways to see the sheer scale of this activity, but driven and walking tours can be just as exciting.
blocks.html: For the famous river crossing, plan your visit in July and August. Our tip: a hot air balloon safari is one of the best ways to take in the full scale of it all, though walking and driving tours can be every bit as exciting.
